identity.title: Kernel shell-startup issuer: process-root, generation-bound, renderer-only authority for device.gpu.shell

context_capsule.purpose_for_a_reader_without_history: The trusted process root of the new Vulkan shell can mint one non-cloneable, non-serializable authority value, bound to actual process birth, shell generation and a renderer-only purpose, that is the only thing satisfying the shell's StartupRefusal::NoDeviceAuthority gate. Without it the product shell binary refuses to open the graphics device (exit 7); only test binaries run.

specification_anchor_refs.paraphrase_from_draft: Pre-account render only under the exact registered full capability device.gpu.shell (verbatim text in MT-219.json#/context_capsule/specification_anchor_refs).
No caller-supplied identity, serialized state, registry label, capability string or liveness lease creates authority; no account, Principal, session or audit event is fabricated.
Negative tests for forge, clone, replay, deserialize and stale handle.
Shutdown, retirement or replacement denies new admissions; in-flight GPU ownership stays with the original owner until settlement.
Defines required semantics, not an implemented API; the trust-port binding is supplied by the host runtime authority owner and the reusable renderer owner.
Missing reusable trust-port mechanics go through canonical source, proof, publication, reread and a distinct exact-pinned adoption first.

closure_unit.outcome: A non-cloneable, non-serializable authority value that only the trusted process root can mint, bound to actual process birth, shell generation, renderer-only purpose and lifecycle, with revocation and denial after retirement; the shell's StartupRefusal::NoDeviceAuthority gate is satisfied by it and by nothing else.

materialized_acceptance.text: Authority type: the authority value is not Clone, Copy, Default, Serialize or Deserialize and has no public constructor; the only mint path takes a process-root proof created once at process birth. Compile-fail tests prove each of clone, copy, default, serialize, deserialize and direct construction does not compile outside the issuer crate.

Registry binding: before arming, the issuer consumes the verified published registry entry (registry version digest and the exact device.gpu.shell entry published by MT-219) and arms only when digest and entry match; a missing file, missing entry, altered entry or digest mismatch leaves issuance unavailable with a typed refusal, tested for each case (handback-02 native_pre_effect_check).

Forge resistance: caller-supplied identity, serialized state, registry label, capability string and liveness lease cannot create authority; tests cover forge, replay of a prior value, deserialize attempt and stale handle (a handle from a retired generation) and each yields a typed denial (NATIVE-RENDER-BOOT-002, -003).

Lifecycle: shutdown, retirement or replacement of the shell generation revokes the value and denies every new admission after it; in-flight GPU ownership stays with the original MT-203 owner until its settlement, and the issuer neither settles nor releases it (NATIVE-RENDER-BOOT-005, -006). Tested with an in-flight claim at retirement.

No fabricated identity: issuance and denial create no account, Principal, session or audit event and never invent pre-account attribution; attribution is the process instance and shell generation only (NATIVE-RENDER-BOOT-002).

Registered is not granted: CapabilityRegistry::can_perform still returns false for device.gpu.shell for every profile, role, model, account and string, and the existing test capabilities::tests::test_shell_gpu_capability_is_not_grantable_by_strings_or_profiles still passes unchanged.

Shell gate: through the single named hand-over of src/frontend/handshake_shell/shell/src/authority.rs, run_product refuses with StartupRefusal::NoDeviceAuthority (exit 7) without the issuer's value and passes that gate with it; the shell crate has no other way to build an authority value; test binaries keep declaring their no-authority mode in their receipts.

Independent verdict: the denial tests of AC222-1 to AC222-5 are reviewed or extended by an agent that did not write the issuer; the author's own tests are not the sole proof (GLOBAL-CLOSURE-042 separation).

Scope: the issuer only. No change to capabilities.rs grants, profiles or sessions, to the registry file (MT-219), to vulkan-renderer/** (MT-203) or to Master Spec text, and no Vulkan call, quota ledger or account-session authority is added.

Reusable mechanics: no reusable trust-port mechanic is implemented in this MT. Any such mechanic found missing at S1 is added first through a distinct standalone-source MT in its canonical asset repository, re-read and pinned, and this crate only adapts it (NATIVE-RENDER-BOOT-008, CX-MODULE-LIFECYCLE-002); the host-side issuer stays a Handshake adaptation.
